topic: Why does your phone get hot?
title: Your Phone Is Secretly a Tiny Heater 🔥
description: Almost all the power your phone's chip uses ends up as heat — and phones have no fan to blow it away.
Graphite sheets and vapor chambers spread it into the case; if that's not enough, the phone slows itself down.
sources: Android Central – Tech Talk: why does my phone get hot?: https://www.androidcentral.com/phones/tech-talk-why-does-my-phone-get-hot

beats.narration: Your phone is a tiny *heater* that happens to make calls.
Almost all the power your chip uses ends up as *heat*.
Electricity flows through billions of tiny switches, and every switch sheds a little warmth.
The hottest spots: the chip, the battery while charging, and the screen.
That's why it warms up most when you game, film video, or charge it.
And unlike a laptop, your phone has *no fan* to push that heat out.
So it spreads heat through graphite sheets, and in some phones vapor chambers, into the case.
If it still runs too hot, it *slows itself down* on purpose to cool off.
